scenes.vo: Anthropic's staff expect AI to do 75% of their job by 2030.

scenes.shot: wide, static: a crowd crossing a junction (the two crowds polled)
scenes.vo: In August Anthropic ran one questionnaire on two crowds: 10,980 American adults and 1,334 of its own staff. A Nobel-level discovery by 2030? 39% of Americans. 91% of staff.

scenes.shot: medium: a man alone at his desk at night (the personal question)
scenes.sub: share of their own working hours AI could do by 2030
scenes.vo: Then the personal question. Employed Americans say AI could do 28% of their own working hours by 2030. Staff say 75%. More than half say 80% or above.

scenes.sub: of staff expect headcount to grow in the next 12 months. Median guess: +66%
scenes.vo: The same staff: 95% expect headcount to grow over the next 12 months. The median guess is 66%. 27% expect it to double.

scenes.shot: close: a stack of printed pages (the report's own line)
scenes.big: “Automating tasks and shedding jobs are different forecasts, at least at a frontier AI lab.”
scenes.vo: Personal expectations, not a plan, the authors say. And add: automating tasks and shedding jobs are different forecasts, at least at a frontier AI lab. At least. Hold that.

scenes.shot: wide, static: office lights row by row (generated), then night avenues from above (unemployment)
labels: 2030, says the group expecting AI to take 80%+ of their work
scenes.vo: Everyone was told unemployment is 4.2% and asked for 2030. Those who expect AI to take 80% or more of their work say 12.2%, above the 2009 peak. Over half of staff are in that group.

scenes.shot: abstract: smoke on black (a crisis number)
scenes.big: For us, hiring. For everyone else, a number last seen in a financial crisis.
scenes.vo: So the forecast from inside the lab reads: for us, hiring; for everyone else, a number last seen in a financial crisis.

scenes.shot: close, static: server rack lights (agent hours)

scenes.vo: In March the agents' working hours passed the humans'. By August, six to one.
